advice: Propose an exact, bounded cache-set padding experiment in the existing full512 kernel. Keep one LIBXSMM call and its 64-row output traversal. In the `Llibxsmm_78` A-panel packing loop, store each K slice at a 272-byte stride: 64 FP32 values (256 bytes) followed by 4 FP32 padding values (16 bytes). Allocate 512 × 272 = 139,264 bytes (136 KiB) per active panel. Update both compute loops (`Llibxsmm_478` and `Llibxsmm_70c`) to advance the packed-A pointer by 272 bytes per K step and rewind it by 512 × 272 bytes after the loop. Keep the B stride, output traversal, FMOPA order, logical packed values, and general-size fallback unchanged. Hypothesis: the 16-byte stride shift may change scratch cache-set mapping and reduce conflicts on Apple M4 Pro; the supplied evidence does not establish cache geometry or that this will help. Advice only; implementation and performance are unverified.
risks: The padded allocation adds 8 KiB over the original 128 KiB panel, and padding/address updates may cost more than any locality gain. This proposal replaces the earlier inconsistent 2,112-byte stride: 512 FP32 values plus 32 padding values would be 2,176 bytes per slice, while a 2,112-byte stride cannot hold 544 FP32 values. Keep the 272-byte stride consistent in allocation, pack destination, both consumers, and rewinds; verify all 512 slices fit and that no padding value is consumed. Check full GEMM at n=512 plus general sizes, tails, n<=0, and tolerance 0.002. Measure complete timed calls, including allocation and packing, against fresh paired controls with power mode and settings unchanged; report spreads and do not infer cache causality from noisy results.
